stories.headline: Carly Rae Jepsen and Lena Dunham’s ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Sets Broadway Start Date - The Hollywood Reporter
stories.summary: The production features music and lyrics by Jepsen and Ethan Gruska and a book by Dunham and playwright Jessica Huang, with Christopher Wheeldon directing and choreographing.
stories.why: Lena Dunham and Carly Rae Jepsen bringing pop sensibility to prestige theater signals Broadway's shift toward Gen X/millennial cultural references—if this lands, expect more IP adaptations targeting men who grew up on '90s teen comedies but now consume Broadway.

stories.headline: Sikoa stays Solo Dolo, has unreal aura, Bloodline in shambles - Cageside Seats
stories.summary: A lot happened in the main event of Monday Night Raw this week, y’all.
stories.why: Solo Sikoa's rise as a credible solo threat (not just riding his family name) mirrors the larger wrestling narrative of 2024: the Anoa'i family's dominance is fragmenting, which matters to wrestling fans tracking power dynamics and who'll actually draw money going forward.

stories.headline: Tupac's murder was act of revenge, prosecutors allege in trial's opening day - BBC
stories.summary: After he was shot multiple times, Tupac Shakur refused to cooperate with police and told an officer, "We'll take care of it," an officer testified.
stories.why: Tupac's murder finally getting a courtroom verdict after 28 years closes a cultural wound for the men who grew up with hip-hop as their primary identity; Duane 'Keffe D' Davis's conviction validates street justice narratives that shaped an entire generation's worldview.

stories.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Becomes Second-Fastest To Cross $2B WW – Global Top 10 Box Office Update - Deadline
stories.summary: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' crossed the $2B global mark, becoming the second-fastest movie to do so and the eighth to ever cross that benchmark.
stories.why: Spider-Man hitting $2B in record time proves superhero fatigue is selective—audiences will still show up for legacy characters with genuine emotional stakes, signaling that the MCU's problem isn't genre exhaustion but creative bankruptcy.

stories.headline: David F. Sandberg to Direct Horror Movie ‘Mommy’s Home’ For Lionsgate - Variety
stories.summary: David F. Sandberg has been tapped to direct a new psychological horror movie, 'Mommy's Home,' for Lionsgate.
stories.why: Sandberg (Shazam, Aquaman 2) directing Lionsgate's horror IP means studios are betting on directorial voice over franchise formula; for viewers, it's a rare moment where a studio might prioritize creepy atmosphere over sequel-baiting.

stories.headline: Spoiler: Major Match Planned for WWE Sunday Night’s Main Event - Ringside News
stories.summary: WWE appears to be using tonight’s RAW to set up a serious collision for Sunday Night’s Main Event. According to the spoiler rundown for the August 17
stories.why: Raw's setup for Sunday Night Main Event reveals WWE's card-stacking strategy heading into fall—this matters operationally because wrestling's real audience watches spoilers and debates booking decisions; it signals what creative thinks will move merchandise and retention.

stories.headline: The End Of Oak Street's Box Office Proves One Thing About Dinosaur Movies - SlashFilm
stories.summary: We have the box office results for The End of Oak Street's opening weekend, and they reaffirm a hard truth when it comes to dinosaur movies.
stories.why: A dinosaur movie flopping confirms what studios refuse to admit: the dinosaur IP well is dry unless it's Jurassic World's recognizable cast, meaning original creature-feature pitches are functionally dead in theatrical—streaming is the only viable home for non-franchise monster movies.
